title: Accuracy Assessment of GPR Depth Estimation for Buried PVC Water Pipes in Sandy Loam Soils

record.title: Accuracy Assessment of GPR Depth Estimation for Buried PVC Water Pipes in Sandy Loam Soils
record.abstract: Ground-penetrating radar depth estimates for buried polyvinyl chloride water pipes depend strongly on the dielectric permittivity of the surrounding soil, which varies with moisture content and texture. This study presents controlled-trench experiments carried out at two test sites in Vojvodina, where 110 mm and 160 mm diameter PVC pipes were buried at known depths between 0.6 m and 1.8 m in sandy loam. A 400 MHz antenna was used with a GSSI SIR-3000 system. Permittivity was estimated by the common-midpoint method and cross-validated against time-domain reflectometry probes inserted at five depths per trench. Depth errors for the 400 MHz antenna ranged from 2.1% to 8.7%, with the largest errors occurring when volumetric water content exceeded 28%. A correction procedure based on a two-layer dielectric model reduced mean absolute depth error from 6.3 cm to 2.1 cm. Results indicate that routine moisture monitoring at GPR survey sites can substantially improve cadastral positioning accuracy for utility pipes.
